title: Sampled token-level telemetry and regional failover explorer
creator: Lena Ortiz
description:
Goal: produce a lightweight, production-safe token-level telemetry pipeline using probabilistic sampling that feeds a cross-region dashboard and automated failover signals. This ticket covers instrumentation, sampling heuristics, aggregation, and a dashboard explorer to surface token-latency skew, KV-cache correlation, and circuit-breaker trigger candidates.

Why: full token-level traces are too high-volume to retain at scale. We need representative, explainable SLI derivations (p50/p95/p99 on per-request and per-token basis) that tie back to operational actions (admit thresholds, regional failover triggers, and progressive shed policies).

Acceptance criteria:
- A sampling client library shipped in runtime that implements reservoir + stratified probabilistic sampling for tokens (by route, model, shard, region).
- Aggregation pipeline that emits time-decayed quantiles and count-weighted histograms every 10s for ingestion into metrics store (no raw token payloads retained).
- Dashboard "Failover Explorer" with: stacked token-latency heatmap by region, KV-hit vs miss overlay, recovered SLI derivation panel (p50/p95/p99), and circuit-breaker candidate thresholds with simulated impact slider.
- End-to-end tests: synthetic canary that generates traffic profiles (short, long, KV-heavy) and validates telemetry fidelity within 5% against full-trace baseline in staging.
- Runbook section describing how to interpret explorer panels to make mitigation decisions and example rollback steps.

Non-goals: full-fidelity end-to-end trace retention, replacing existing full-request SLI pipelines, or storing request payloads.
updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, and Console teams. Agreed on privacy constraint: no token text stored; only token-level timing/dimensions retained.

2025-02-18: Prototype sampling library checked in (runtime/sampled_telemetry). Uses stratified reservoir by (route, model, region) with per-second budget enforcement. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123

2025-02-20: Decided on aggregation approach: time-decayed t-digest + fixed-bucket histograms for p99 stability. Trade-off: t-digest faster for memory but buckets needed for circuit threshold simulation. Documented on Confluence: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/SLI-sampled
2025-02-24: Telemetry ingestion prototype in staging; initial dashboards in Grafana (panel ids: 121, 124). Observed KV-miss correlation with 30ms tail shift on model/large-seq routes.
2025-02-26: Review feedback from Privacy & Security: add HMAC of request id for correlation, rotate salt daily. Security review flagged—mitigation added as dependency for final rollout.

2025-02-28: SRE requested a synthetic validation harness to compare sampled-derived p95 vs full-trace p95. Draft harness in infra/tests/synth-sli-harness. First run: sample pipeline within 7% of baseline on mixed workload.
2025-03-01: Scoped dashboard features for M1: heatmap, kv overlay, p95/p99 beams, and 'simulate threshold' slider. M2 will add auto-alert recommendation and canary-based automatic threshold tuning.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on sampling bias across low-volume routes and privacy compliance. Suggested checklist: (1) verify no token text persisted, (2) confirm HMAC salt rotation, (3) validate t-digest parameters for p99 stability.
runbook_excerpt: When p95 deviates >15% in one region vs baseline: 1) open Failover Explorer and compare KV overlay; 2) if KV-miss spike present, enable conservative shed for affected route (admit cap -20%); 3) if network latency spike present, trigger regional failover per failover playbook; 4) escalate to on-call runtime if feed-forward mitigation doesn't reduce p95 within 5 minutes.
